items.headline: Japanese grandmothers hand-stitch a rare Air Jordan 1
items.caption: The Sashiko Gals turned a colette Jordan into a one-off.
body: Only about 213 pairs of the colette Jordan 1 were made in 2017.
The 15-woman collective, aged 40 to 80, covered one in colourful sashiko stitching.
How to wear it: keep it on a shelf, honestly.

items.headline: Romeo Beckham's road-trip denim for Tommy Jeans
items.caption: Lived-in denim and big outerwear for the winter campaign.
body: He fronts Tommy Jeans' winter 2026 campaign with Yasmin Wijnaldum.
Think plaid, teddy textures and relaxed layers.
How to wear it: worn-in jeans under an oversized coat.

items.headline: Kith turns adidas ballet flats to suede
items.caption: The Stan Smith Ballet gets a cosy winter makeover.
body: It's the first collab on the shoe, in brown suede.
Two colourways drop on 6 November.
How to wear it: with wide trousers and thick socks.

items.headline: Our Legacy on its Nike partnership
items.caption: 'Look slow, feel fast': the cofounder explains what's coming.
body: Our Legacy and Nike have finally confirmed their long-rumoured team-up.
Cofounder Jockum Hallin talks about the first pop-up in New York.
How to wear it: quiet sportswear with good trousers.

items.headline: Nike's Air Max 90 drops the logos
items.caption: A soft-leather version in olive with less branding.
body: The 'Air Max' badge and heel lettering are gone.
Padded panels make it feel more luxurious.
How to wear it: olive chinos and a grey knit.

items.headline: An adidas Samba dressed for dinner
items.caption: Invincible adds brogue details to the football classic.
body: The all-black 'Samba Dress Shoe' adds wingtip punching.
The heel has ruched leather instead of the usual panel.
How to wear it: with a black suit, no tie.

items.headline: The Clarks Wallabee goes hiking
items.caption: Diemme gives it rope laces and a chunky lugged sole.
body: It's made in pale champagne suede.
A mountain Desert Boot and Desert Trek drop too.
How to wear it: with cords and a fleece.

items.headline: A senator-elect's watch-nerd pick
items.caption: Abdul El-Sayed wore a limited Grand Seiko on election night.
body: It is a Spring Drive Chronograph GMT.
GQ calls him the first real watch nerd in the Senate.
Style lesson: one good watch says more than five.

items.headline: Tom Hardy's case for a trench coat
items.caption: Black for big nights, navy for dinner, tan for everything.
body: Hardy has worn trenches on press tours for years.
Esquire picks nine affordable options.
How to wear it: belted, over a suit or a hoodie.

items.headline: Casio's £290 mechanical field watch
items.caption: The CMK-100 looks like a Rolex Explorer for a fraction of the price.
body: It's Casio's first mainline automatic watch.
It has a 38mm titanium case.
How to wear it: on a canvas strap, every day.

items.headline: Seiko made watches for Hideo Kojima fans
items.caption: Two limited watches for Kojima Productions' tenth anniversary.
body: They're inspired by the studio's spacesuit mascot, Ludens.
Only 300 of each colour, sold in Japan.
Style lesson: let a fun watch be the only loud thing.

items.headline: Church's turns a London pub into a shoe club
items.caption: A night of British shoes, gin and heritage in Marylebone.
body: Church's hosted 'Church's Club' at The Hart pub.
Think rustic rooms, gin tastings and very good shoes.
How to wear it: polished brogues with tweed.

items.headline: Brazil enlarges a Pantanal national park by a third
items.caption: 185 more square miles of the world's largest tropical wetland protected.
body: The park grew from 523 to over 700 square miles.
The Pantanal is home to jaguars, giant otters and hundreds of bird species.

items.headline: First person to swim the whole California coast
items.caption: Catherine Breed swam 900 miles in 111 days.
body: She faced storms, tough currents and 8 shark encounters.
She has also swum the English Channel.

items.headline: Houston students open a public auto shop
items.caption: High schoolers change your oil while learning a trade.
body: The shop in Houston's Fifth Ward is run by the Barbara Jordan Career Center.
The centre serves over 1,200 students from 12 campuses.
